realLife: Spam filters have long used naive Bayes because it is fast and accurate enough, even though its percentages are rough.
summary: Multiply simple per-feature evidence as if features did not influence each other.
headline: Fast, simple and overconfident
overview: Naive Bayes estimates how each feature looks within each class, then multiplies those pieces together. The word naive is the assumption that features are independent once the class is known.
It often classifies well. Its probabilities are another matter: duplicated evidence gets counted again and again.

break.label: Break it
break.explains: Copy the first feature eight times. Nothing new was learned, yet the model becomes far more confident while accuracy barely changes.

check.question: Why do copied features make naive Bayes overconfident?
options: It counts the same evidence repeatedly
It switches to a different formula

data: Two numeric features per point and a Gaussian model for each feature within each class. The slider copies feature one, standing in for correlated columns.
maths: Each copy of a feature adds another identical factor, which pushes the product toward 0 or 1.
code:
from sklearn.naive_bayes import GaussianNB
m = GaussianNB().fit(X, y)
m.predict_proba(X_new)

sources.title: scikit-learn: naive Bayes
